questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png]

 ×

Given expression : 36 A (15 C 4) B (21 A 13) A 24 D (16 D 2) = ?

After replacing the given symbols in place of alphabets the expression is as follows : 36 + (15 × 4) - (21 + 13) + 24 ÷ (16 ÷ 2)

= 36 + __**(15 × 4)**__ - __**(21 + 13)**__ + 24 ÷ __**(16 ÷ 2)**__

= 36 + 60 - 34 + __**24 ÷ 8**__

= __**36 + 60**__ - 34 __**+ 3**__

= __**99 - 34**__

=** ****65**

Hence, the correct answer is **"65".**

questions.question: Under the ______ system of land revenue, the ownership rights were handed over to the peasants and the British Government collected taxes directly from them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ryotwari.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Under the Ryotwari system of land revenue, the ownership rights were handed over to the peasants and the British government collected taxes directly from them.**
 
• At the end of the 18th century, **Captain Alexander Read and Sir Thomas Munro** developed a system that later came to be known as the Ryotwari System. Sir Thomas Munro then implemented it while serving as governor of the** Madras Presidency (1819–26)**. Under the Ryotwari system, the land revenue was paid by the farmers directly to the state.
 
• In this system, an individual cultivator by the** name of Ryot** had complete rights over the purchase, transfer, and leasing of land.
 
• The ryots could not be evicted from their land as long as they paid the rent.
 
• It was** prevalent in most of southern India, first introduced in Tamil Nadu.**
 
• Later, it was extended to Assam, Berar, East Punjab, Coorg, and Maharashtra.
 
• The advantages of this system were the elimination of middlemen, who often oppressed villagers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalwari System**

 
 
• In **1822**, Englishman Holt Mackenzie introduced a new system known as the Mahalwari System in the North Western Provinces of the Bengal Presidency **(most of this area is now in Uttar Pradesh).**
 
• **Lord William Bentick **popularized the system in Agra and Awadh before expanding it to Madhya Pradesh and Punjab.
 
 
 
• **Malguzari System**
 
 
• The land tenure triumphing withinside the erstwhile Central Provinces changed into referred to as** Malguzari device** wherein the Malguzar changed into simply a sales farmer below the Marathas.
 
• Under the Malguzari system, the Lambardar/Sadar Lambardar appointed from amongst the Malguzars, was once the income engager.
 
 
 
• **Taluqdar System**
 
 
• The time period ‘**taluqdar**’ has unique meanings in exceptional components of India. In Oudh, taluqdar is a extraordinary landholder.
 
• But in Bengal, a taluqdar is subsequent to zamindar in extent of land manage and social status.
 
• The large zamindars themselves had created many taluqs underneath countless denominations, such as, junglburi taluq, mazkuri taluq, shikimi taluq, and so on.

questions.question: Which of the following is another name for Vitamin K1?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Phylloquinone.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phylloquinone is another name for Vitamin K1.**
 
• **Vitamin K1 is a fat soluble vitamin used to treat hemorrhagic conditions in infants and coumarin overdoses.**
 
• Vitamin K1, also called phylloquinone or phytonadione, is a** fat soluble vitamin.**
 
• Phylloquinone is a cofactor of the enzyme γ-carboxylase, which modifies and activates precursors to coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X.
 
• It is indicated in the treatment of coagulation disorders due to faulty formation of coagulation factors II, VII, IX, and X caused by deficiency or interference in the activity of vitamin K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__** Nicotinic acid**__

__
 
• Niacin, also known as nicotinic acid and vitamin B3, is a water soluble, essential B vitamin that, when given in high doses, is effective in lowering low density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and raising high density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, which makes this agent of unique value in the therapy of dyslipidemia.
 
• Niacin can cause mild-to-moderate serum aminotransferase elevations and high doses and certain formulations of niacin have been linked to clinically apparent, acute liver injury which can be severe as well as fatal.

**Thiamine**__

__
 
• Thiamin (thiamine), or vitamin B1, is a water-soluble vitamin found naturally in some foods, added to foods, and sold as a supplement. Thiamin plays a vital role in the growth and function of various cells.
 
• Only small amounts are stored in the liver, so a daily intake of thiamin-rich foods is needed.

**Riboflavin**__

 
• Vitamin B2, or riboflavin, is naturally present in foods, added to foods, and available as a supplement. Bacteria in the gut can produce small amounts of riboflavin, but not enough to meet dietary needs.
 
• Riboflavin is a key component of coenzymes involved with the growth of cells, energy production, and the breakdown of fats, steroids, and medications.

questions.question: 6 April 1919 was observed as a day of non-violent opposition to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** The Rowlatt Act.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **6 April 1919 was observed as a day of non-violent opposition to the Rowlatt Act.**
 
• On 6 April 1919, Mahatma Gandhi started a non-violent Satyagraha against the unjust Rowlatt Act passed by the British government.
 
• The Rowlatt Act was the popular name for the **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919 passed by the British Indian government.**
 
• This Act was termed the** ‘Black Act’ **by the Indian public because of its unjust and restrictive nature. The Act was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council on 18th March 1919.
 
• It basically extended the **emergency provisions imposed by the 1915 Defence of India Act **that was passed during the First World War.
 
• The Act gave the **government the power to imprison any person suspected of terrorist activities for a maximum period of two years without trial.**
 
• This was known as the** Rowlatt Satyagraha and April 6th was the designated date for the hartal to begin**. People would refrain from going to work and hold meetings against the repressive act.
 
• The government clamped down heavily on the people. There were violent clashes in many parts.
 
• Two Congress leaders** Dr. Satya Pal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew were arrested**. The army was deployed in Punjab where martial law was enacted.
 
• The** infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in Amritsar on 13th April 1919. **The people had gathered at the enclosed garden to celebrate Baisakhi and also to condemn the arrest of the two leaders.
 
• C**olonel Reginald Dyer **arrived there with his troops and without warning fired upon the unarmed crowd.
 
• **In March 1922, the Rowlatt Act and 22 other acts were repealed by the government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**The Simon Commission**__

__
 
• Simon Commission was the Indian Statutory Commission, which was a group of seven Members of Parliament under the chairmanship of Sir John Simon.
 
• The commission arrived in British India in 1928 to study constitutional reform in Britain’s largest and most important possession.
 
• The Government of India Act of 1919 provided for the appointment of a commission to study the progress of the governance scheme and suggest new steps after ten years Since the British administration had failed to include even a single Indian in the Commission, it was strongly opposed by national leaders and freedom.

**The Cabinet Mission Plan**__

__
 
• Cabinet Mission was a high-powered mission sent in February 1946 to India by the Atlee Government (British Prime Minister.) The mission had three British cabinet members – Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, & and A.V. Alexander.
 
• The Cabinet Mission’s aim was to discuss the transfer of power from British to Indian leadership.
 
• **Objectives of Cabinet Mission** -To obtain an agreement with the Indian leaders as to the framing of a constitution for India.
 
• To formulate a constitution-making body (the Constituent Assembly of India)
 
• To establish an Executive Council with the support of the major Indian parties.

**The Morely-Minto Reforms**__

 
• The Indian Councils Act 1909 was an act of the British Parliament that introduced a few reforms in the legislative councils and increased the involvement of Indians (limited) in the governance of British India.
 
• It was more commonly called the Morley-Minto Reforms after the Secretary of State for India John Morley and the Viceroy of India, the 4th Earl of Minto
 
• The legislative councils at the Centre and the provinces increased in size.
 
• Indians were given membership to the Imperial Legislative Council for the first time.
 
• It introduced separate electorates for the Muslims. 
 
• The members could discuss the budget and move resolutions. They could also discuss matters of public interest.
 
• They could also ask supplementary questions. No discussions on foreign policy or on relations with the princely states were permitted.
 
• Lord Minto appointed (on much persuasion by Morley) Satyendra P Sinha as the first Indian member of the Viceroy’s Executive Council.
 
• Two Indians were nominated to the Council of the Secretary of State for Indian affairs.

questions.question: Train A passes an electric pole in 15 seconds, moving at 60 kmh. It crosses train B moving in the opposite direction at 48 km/h, in 19 seconds. What is the length (in m) of train B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Length of Train A = Speed × Time = (60 × 5/18) × 15 = 250 m

Relative speed (opposite direction) = (60 + 48) × 5/18 = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

Total distance (Length of Train A + Length of Train B) = Relative speed × Time = 30 × 19 = 570 m

Length of Train B = 570 − 250 = 320 m

**∴ The correct answer is 320 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Train A (SA) = 60 km/h

Time taken by Train A to cross an electric pole = 15 s

Speed of Train B (SB) = 48 km/h

Time taken by both trains to cross each other = 19 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Relative Speed (opposite directions) = SA + SB

**Calculations:**

 
• 
 
 
 Train A
 60 km/h →
 Length = 250 m
 
 
 Train B
 ← 48 km/h
 Length = ?
 
 Relative Speed = 108 km/h | Time = 19 s

⇒ Speed of Train A in m/s = 60 × 5/18 = 50/3 m/s

⇒ Length of Train A (LA) = Speed × Time = (50/3) × 15 = 250 m

⇒ Relative speed of Train A and Train B = 60 + 48 = 108 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

⇒ Total distance covered during crossing = LA + LB

⇒ Total Distance = Relative speed × Time

⇒ 250 + LB = 30 × 19

⇒ 250 + LB = 570

⇒ LB = 570 − 250 = 320 m

**∴ The correct answer is 320 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses a stationary object of negligible length (like an electric pole or a standing man), the distance traveled is equal to the length of the train itself. When crossing another train or a platform, the distance traveled is the sum of their lengths: L₁ + L₂.
